title: Dedicated capacity discovery - Sable Bank
next_steps: Send dedicated capacity pricing and TCO spreadsheet
Share SOC 2 / compliance pack and network docs
Schedule 2-4 hour benchmark run on sample workload with Redwood Dedicated (SE to own)
Follow-up call for benchmark results and pricing review week of 2026-03-09
action_items: Jordan Lee: send pricing + TCO by 2026-03-06
Priya Raman: prepare benchmark run plan and reagents (env details) by 2026-03-05
Samir Gupta (Sable): provide sample prompt set and peak concurrency profile by 2026-03-05
transcript:
[15:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood Inference, I'm AE for this region. We also have Priya from our solutions engineering team. Quick intro around objectives, we want to understand your inference needs and see if Dedicated makes sense vs Hosted or Private
[15:10] Marcus: Thanks, Jordan. I'm Marcus, I run ML infra at Sable. We have Rita and Samir here. High level we run a bunch of LLM features across internal products — chat, summarization, and some embeddings. We're evaluating options for predictable latency and data isolation, so Dedicated is top of mind.
[15:22] Rita: timeline is Q2 pilot, production in Q3 if everything looks good. Budget conversations are upcoming.
[15:28] Jordan: great, we'll try to qualify on traffic, latency, security, and success criteria. Priya, do you want to kick us off on technical Qs?
[15:33] Priya: sure. Marcus, can you paint the current architecture? Where do models run today and what GPUs, roughly?
[15:40] Marcus: today we host most inference in-house on AWS EC2 G5s for some heavy models and we also use a mix of lambda-style hosted endpoints for lightweight tasks. We're seeing inconsistent latencies during peak, and utilization spikes are causing throttling. For large generation we use A100s in some pockets.
[15:53] Samir: we prefer reserved capacity where possible. We need isolation — customer data and some transcripts are regulated. Sable is subject to regional data residency rules for EU customers.
[16:01] Jordan: got it, so isolation and predictable capacity are requirements — sounds like Dedicated or Private. Any constraints re: network? VPC peering, or do you need a private control plane?
[16:09] Samir: we prefer VPC peering and ability to use our KMS for keys. We don't want logs leaving our audit domain.
[16:14] Priya: Redwood Dedicated supports VPC peering and customer-managed KMS integrations; audit logs can be exported to your cloud logging. For Private (on-prem) we can support an air-gapped setup but that's longer lead time.
[16:27] Rita: curious on burst strategy — our traffic is spiky with peaks 3x baseline for a few hours a day. How does Dedicated handle burst?
[16:34] Jordan: two approaches: reserved capacity for base load and burst to hosted pool or pre-warmed spare nodes for scheduled peaks. You can configure burst policies — automatic fallback to compatible model variants on hosted pool or use burst capacity owned by the Dedicated contract.
[16:46] Marcus: ok, price delta between reserved vs burst is important. Also how autoscaling works — do we pay for idle GPUs if reserved?
[16:52] Priya: reserved capacity commits guarantee baseline throughput; you pay commit for reserved units. Autoscaling within dedicated pool can add more GPUs from the reserved pool without reconfiguration; idle resources within the reserved allocation count toward the commit. For cost control we recommend right-sized commits + short-term burst from hosted where latency tolerant.
[17:06] Jordan: note there's also model optimization — quantization and packing can materially reduce GPU needs. We can show recommendations after we see your prompt distribution.
[17:14] Samir: how granular is model pinning and rollouts? We need canary and A/B for models to prevent regression.
[17:19] Priya: Redwood supports model pinning per route, canary rollouts, automatic fallback to previous versions and to cheaper variants if SLOs breach. We have tracing and per-token cost dashboards in Console.
[17:29] Rita: about latency — our SLO is 200-300ms p95 for short completions, longer for multi-turn chat is ok. What realistic latencies do you hit?
[17:36] Priya: depends on model + seq length. For trimmed T5-style small models under Dedicated on modern GPUs we see sub-100ms p95 single-turn. For large 70B/LLMs it depends — tens to hundreds of ms per token. We'll capture your full workload in the benchmark.
[17:48] Marcus: security — SOC 2, SSO/SAML and RBAC are must-haves. Also audit trails and KMS.
[17:53] Jordan: we have SOC 2 and can share the compliance pack; SAML SSO and RBAC supported, and Dedicated includes audit log export. For customer-managed KMS and HSM, we integrate via key proxies — some customers require Private for HSM direct attach.
[18:06] Samir: does Redwood store any customer prompts or payloads in hosted fallback? We need guarantees for logs and retention.
[18:12] Priya: for Dedicated we can configure retention policies; hosted fallback can be configured to not persist transcripts; we'll align the data flow and endpoints with your legal team.
[18:21] Rita: integration complexity — how much work to onboard? We run on AWS — do you provide deployment manifests?
[18:27] Priya: yes, for Dedicated we provide Terraform modules, k8s manifests for private deployments, and we handle the control plane setup. For Dedicated in cloud we operate the runtime but peered into your VPC. Typical onboarding 2-6 weeks depending on security review.
[18:40] Marcus: if we run a pilot, what do we need to provide?
[18:44] Priya: sample prompt set, payload sizes, expected concurrency, and representative models. We'll run a benchmark that exercises p95 latency, concurrency and token throughput — we recommend 2-4 hours for meaningful numbers.
[18:56] Jordan: we'll also include cost projection for reserved vs hosted burst and the TCO.
[19:01] Marcus: what about model support — do you host open models or custom models? We have fine-tuned internal models.
[19:06] Priya: we host curated open models and can bring-your-own models; for private/custom models we support packaging and quantization. We'll need to validate licensing and weights — some storage constraints apply.
[19:16] Rita: any pitfalls customers see switching from self-hosted to Dedicated?
[19:19] Jordan: common items are underestimating peak concurrency and KV cache hit patterns; also networking (e.g., latency to VPC subnets). We instrument those in the benchmark.
[19:27] Samir: can you describe KV cache / prefix cache behavior? We rely on long conversational context and caching matters.
[19:33] Priya: Redwood runtime has KV cache sharing per session and supports prefix caching for repeated system prompts, reducing tokens per request. We'll capture your distribution to suggest cache warmers and batching strategies.
[19:44] Marcus: SLA — what uptime/latency guarantees for Dedicated?
[19:47] Jordan: Dedicated customers get SLA-backed uptime and latency targets that can be included in the contract; for hard SLOs we have options for redundancy across AZs or regions.
[19:56] Rita: legal/procurement timing — we might need details for procurement to evaluate.
[19:59] Jordan: we'll send procurement checklist and standard contract template.
[20:03] Samir: curious on observability — what dashboards and logs we get?
[20:07] Priya: Console includes per-route latency/cost breakdown, token-level traces, error rates, and per-model throughput. Logs can be streamed to your cloud logging or S3.
[20:16] Marcus: ok great. Anything else on network encryption and HSM?
[20:21] Jordan: all in transit is TLS; at rest can be customer-managed KMS. HSM support typically via Private/on-prem or vendor-managed HSM proxy for Dedicated. We'll detail options in the compliance pack.
[20:33] Rita: decision criteria — for our execs we care about predictable unit cost, security certifications, and ramp speed. If you can show a pilot with clear TCO and SLA, we can move forward.
[20:44] Jordan: understood. We'll follow up with the items listed. Priya, any recommendations for initial sizing?
[20:49] Priya: based on what we heard: baseline reserved capacity for average QPS with headroom for 1.5x, and configure burst to hosted pool for unexpected peaks. Start with a 4-GPU equivalent reservation (A100-equivalent) for pilot, then scale after benchmark. We'll provide exact sizing after we see sample prompts and concurrency.
[21:05] Marcus: sounds reasonable. We'll aim to share artifacts by Thursday.
[21:09] Samir: also to confirm, can you run a short canary with our fine-tuned model?
[21:13] Priya: yes, we can include your model in the pilot; we'll need the weights and a data access agreement for validation.
[21:20] Jordan: recap — next steps: Jordan to send pricing/TCO and contract checklist; Priya to schedule benchmark and prepare run plan; Samir to share sample prompts and traffic profile; follow-up call week of 2026-03-09 to review results.
[21:32] Rita: thanks everyone.
[21:33] Jordan: thanks all, we'll send links to the SOC2 pack and the benchmark template — links: https://redwood.example.com/compliance/sable-pack (placeholder), https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/sable-template (placeholder)
[21:40] End of recording
